title: canary-rollout-scratchpad-grace-chen
body:
Scratchpad: canary rollout notes (working doc)

Context:
- Purpose: roll out runtime v2.3.1 (performance + KV-cache fix) to hosted API canary.
- Goal: validate latency regressions, memory stability, and no increase in error rate before wider rollout to Dedicated.
- Owner: Grace Chen (release-engineering) — escalate to Samir if infra/resource issues.

High-level plan / ramp schedule (proposed):
- Day 0: deploy v2.3.1 to canary pool (5% of traffic) in us-west-2 only, pinned to model-variants compatible with kernel set A.
- Day 1: monitor 12–24h; if stable, increase to 20% (us-west-2 + us-east-1 limited).
- Day 2: 50% traffic if gating metrics green for 24h.
- Day 3–4: full roll to all regions with staged Dedicated migrations starting for high-traffic customers.
- Fast rollback: if any gating metric fails at any step, revert to v2.3.0 for canary pool and halt ramp.

Traffic routing / pinning notes:
- Use pin-by-header for internal test clients (X-Redwood-Test: canary) to direct 1% internal traffic for extra load testing.
- Pin model versions: lock to model v1.8.2 on canary to avoid model-agnostic behavior changes.
- Ensure fallback policy configured: if v2.3.1 instance unavailable, route to v2.3.0 (same region).

Gating criteria (must be met to escalate):
- Latency P95 <= baseline P95 + 10% (baseline = v2.3.0 14-day median).
- Error rate (5xx + timeout) <= baseline + 0.1%.
- Memory OOM events = 0 for 48h on canary nodes.
- Token-per-second cost not increased by >5% after batching changes.
- No new regressions in sampling quality (smoke prompt set pass rate >= 98%).

Smoke tests and health checks:
- Run smoke suite every 10m against canary pool (script: infra/canary-smoke.sh).
- Synthetic prompts: short-gen, long-gen (2k tokens), streaming, embeddings. Check output length sanity and latency.
- KV cache hit-rate dashboard: ensure hit-rate does not drop >15% (indicative of cache key change).
- Model-quality quick-check: run 200 prompt evals from evals/canary-set, compare similarity scores.

Monitoring dashboards & alerts (who to notify):
- Dashboards: /dashboards/canary/latency, /dashboards/canary/errors, /dashboards/canary/memory.
- Alerts: PagerDuty on-call (SRE) if 5xx > 0.5% for 10m, or P95 latency > threshold for 30m.
- Slack channel: #releases (primary), #sre-escalation (backup).
- Notify product and customer success if canary affects any monitored enterprise customers.

Rollback plan:
- Trigger: any gating criteria fail or manual hit from on-call.
- Steps: 1) Pause new canary traffic. 2) Re-route active canary sessions to v2.3.0. 3) Force drain and decommission canary nodes for v2.3.1. 4) Run post-rollback validation for 1h.
- Postmortem owner: Grace -> handoff to Samir if infra-related; include timeline and logs.

Pre-deploy checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm canary infra capacity (min 3 nodes per region).
- [ ] Build artifacts signed and available in registry (runtime:v2.3.1).
- [ ] Update rollout config and staged traffic policies in Console.
- [ ] Add brief release notes to #releases Slack + tag docs.
- [ ] Coordinate with Customer Success for any high-risk customers.

Post-deploy follow-ups:
- Collect 24h rolling metrics, attach to JIRA-RELEASE-412.
- Run expanded evals (1k prompts) and store artifacts in s3://redwood-release-artifacts/v2.3.1/canary/.
- If stable, open PR to bump dedicated migration plan and schedule Dedicated maintenance windows.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Q: will kernel selection heuristics cause cold-start latency spikes under low-traffic canary? add spike detector.
- Q: need explicit test for streaming-edge-case where chunking switched — add to smoke set.
- TODO: confirm KMS rotation doesn't interfere with canary VM boot.
- TODO: ask product to sign off on sampling/quality thresholds for this release.

Notes / random thoughts:
- Consider a micro-canary with internal clients first (X-Redwood-Canary-Internal) to catch infra-only issues before user traffic.
- If we see small perf regressions but no errors, prefer longer soak at 20% before increasing.
- Keep communication crisp: "Canary v2.3.1 — monitoring for 72h; contact Grace for rollback".

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after deployment dry-run on staging.
